extra.message: The public endpoint POST /api/integration/partner/intake Base64-decodes the X-Intake-State header and passes it to ObjectInputStream.readObject(). Deserialising attacker-controlled bytes enables remote code execution via gadget chains.

extra.message: The admin endpoint POST /api/admin/branches/import-legacy feeds attacker-supplied JSON 'xml' into an unconfigured com.thoughtworks.xstream.XStream.fromXML(). XStream 1.4.11.1 without a security framework allows arbitrary gadget-chain deserialization and remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: Jwts.parserBuilder().build().parseClaimsJwt(assertion) parses an UNSIGNED JWT (unsecured claims) without verifying any signature. The endpoint /api/integration/partner/decision is public, so anyone can forge an assertion with arbitrary sub (application id) and bureauScore claims.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: Stock DocumentBuilderFactory with no hardening (DOCTYPE/external entities not disabled) parses the identity-provider XML response. A malicious response can declare external entities to read local files or perform SSRF (CWE-611).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: GET /api/admin/branches/validate-xml parses the request parameter 'xml' with an unhardened SAXParserFactory (no disallow-doctype-decl, external entities enabled), allowing XXE file disclosure / SSRF.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The request parameter 'wording' is passed directly to Apache Velocity Velocity.evaluate(), so an attacker (an officer) can inject Velocity directives / expression language and execute arbitrary code server-side (SSTI).

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The mb_limit_rule cookie value is evaluated by org.mvel2.MVEL.executeExpression(). MVEL allows method invocation and class access, so a crafted expression gives arbitrary code execution in the context of the banking API.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The CSV 'identifier' value is concatenated directly into an XPath expression: //holder[policyNo='" + identifier + "']. An identifier such as '] | //* | //x[' alters the query and lets the caller read arbitrary nodes from the policy register.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')

extra.message: The admin-supplied employee reference is concatenated into an LDAP search filter (&(objectClass=person)(uid=<employeeRef>)). Unescaped LDAP special characters allow filter manipulation and directory enumeration (LDAP injection). searchDepartment() at line 87 has the same flaw.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')

extra.message: POST /api/admin/audit/export-to-file builds the destination as new File(exportDir, fileName) using the unsanitised request parameter fileName, allowing path traversal and arbitrary file write outside the exports directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: Notification body is rendered with $unsafe{...} (no HTML escaping). Notification bodies are built from user-influenced text (e.g. officer-supplied document-request messages and decision reasons), so an attacker can store script that executes in a victim's browser.

extra.message: POST /api/notifications/bulk-read trusts a client-supplied 'userId' body field instead of using the authenticated principal, so any user can mark another user's notifications as read (IDOR / broken access control).

extra.message: PATCH /api/customer/account copies the request body onto the Account entity with BeanUtils.copyProperties. The form exposes 'kycTier', so a customer can assign themselves an arbitrary (e.g. tier_3) KYC tier, bypassing server-side tier derivation and limits.

extra.message: POST /workspace/context stores attacker-supplied role/email/name directly into the session. SessionAuthFilter then builds the Spring Security principal from these session attributes, so any authenticated user can set role=bank_admin and satisfy hasRole("BANK_ADMIN") on /admin/** (web-tier privilege escalation).

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: Shared-desk session identifiers are generated as sequential 'DESK-' + counter values and looked up from a cookie (mb_desk) as an authentication credential. The predictable, guessable IDs plus POST /workspace/desk accepting an arbitrary role allow a forged desk session to assume a privileged role.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: The document-collection OTP is generated with ThreadLocalRandom, a non-cryptographic PRNG, making the 6-digit code predictable/brute-forceable. Security codes must use SecureRandom.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: AES/CBC is used with a hard-coded all-zero IV (private static final byte[] IV = new byte[16]) and a hard-coded default key (app.envelope.key fallback). The static IV makes the encryption deterministic and malleable, and the default key is public in source.

cwe: CWE-329: Generation of Predictable IV with CBC Mode

extra.message: enrolDeskCredential stores the desk code as an unsalted MD5 digest (deskCredentialHash) as the user's password hash. cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
